raw_response:
I'm 68 this year, and it's just me and my wife working our 5 mu. My back isn't what it used to be, and she's not strong either, so heavy days mean hiring a couple of workers from the village. We've farmed this land for 40 years, and I know every corner of it. I finished middle school, so I can read the fertilizer bags and I listen when the extension guy comes by, but honestly, I mostly go by what I've seen work on my own fields and what Old Wang and the others are doing. Last year the cabbage price was decent, but urea went up again to over 2.5 yuan per jin, and electricity for the well pump keeps rising. With only 5 mu, every yuan matters — I can't afford to waste money on inputs that don't pay back.

My main system is cabbage–longbean–spinach on about 3 mu. I'll plant 1.5 mu of spring cabbage in mid-March using hybrid seeds from the county supply store — about 100 yuan per mu. I learned two years ago not to save my own cabbage seeds; the heads were too loose and I lost money. I'll spread about 1,000 jin of pig manure per mu that I bought from the farm down the road, then put down compound fertilizer as a base and topdress twice with urea when the heads start forming. Total nitrogen around 18–20 kg per mu. Extension says I could push more, but manure is cheaper and I've got to keep cash for medicine and emergencies. I'll irrigate four times and watch for caterpillars and soft rot.

For chili, I've got 1 mu. I'll buy seedlings in early May — about 120 yuan for the mu. Chili is labor-heavy because my wife and I have to pick every few days in peak season. I'll put down manure and compound fertilizer, then topdress when the first flowers set. Maybe 15 kg N total. The big worry is water — chili needs irrigation every 10 days or so in July and August, and that pump electricity adds up. I'll hire two workers for transplanting because I can't bend down like I used to.

Kidney beans — 1 mu of the pole type. I need to put up the sticks, which takes time. Seeds cost about 45 yuan. Beans don't need as much nitrogen because they fix some themselves, so I'll use less urea — maybe 10 kg N per mu — but they need potassium for the pods. I'll irrigate three times, mostly during flowering and pod-fill. I'll spray for pod borers if I see them.

Maize — 1 mu of summer maize, planted right after the early cabbage comes off in mid-June. Tight window, but I've done it for years. Hybrid seeds, about 55 yuan. Maize is simpler — base fertilizer, one topdress at jointing, and irrigate two or three times depending on rain. About 12–15 kg N per mu. Most of this maize is for our own food and the chickens; it doesn't bring much cash, but it keeps us from having to buy grain.

Spinach — 0.5 mu in the fall, planted in late September after the beans finish. Quick crop, about 60 days. Some manure and a bit of urea, maybe 10 kg N. Irrigate two or three times. If the frost comes early I might lose it, but spinach is hardy and the risk is low.

Labor is our biggest constraint. During cabbage transplanting, chili transplanting, and cabbage harvest, I'll hire 2–3 workers for a few days each time. Hired labor is 120 yuan per day now. We try to do all the weeding, watering, and picking ourselves. Total input cost this year will run about 4,800 yuan. That's a big chunk for us, but if cabbage and chili prices hold at the market in Handan, we should clear maybe 8,000–10,000 yuan after costs. Enough to live on, pay for our blood pressure medicine, and save a little against a bad year.
